name: Falklands War

sides.name: United Kingdom
sides.commander: John Fieldhouse (overall, from Northwood), Sandy Woodward (carrier battle group), Julian Thompson (3 Commando Brigade), Jeremy Moore (overall land)
sides.strength: About 30,000 personnel, two aircraft carriers (Hermes and Invincible), Harrier and Sea Harrier squadrons, the 3 Commando and 5th Infantry Brigades
sides.casualties: 255 killed, 775 wounded; 2 destroyers, 2 frigates, and several other ships lost

sides.name: Argentina
sides.commander: Leopoldo Galtieri (junta), Mario Menéndez (military governor of Las Malvinas)
sides.strength: About 11,400 troops on the islands, the carrier Veinticinco de Mayo (kept in port after the Belgrano sank), Mirage and A-4 Skyhawk squadrons
sides.casualties: 649 killed (323 on the cruiser General Belgrano alone), 1,657 wounded; 11,313 captured at the surrender

summary: Argentina's junta seized the British dependency on the second of April hoping to deflect attention from a domestic political crisis. Margaret Thatcher's government dispatched a task force 13,000 kilometres south within three days. The submarine HMS Conqueror sank the cruiser General Belgrano on the second of May. Argentine Super Étendard fighters retaliated with Exocet strikes that sank HMS Sheffield two days later. British troops landed at San Carlos Water on the twenty-first of May, fought a series of battles eastward across East Falkland (Goose Green, Mount Longdon, Tumbledown), and accepted the Argentine surrender at Port Stanley on the fourteenth of June.
significance: The Falklands War saved Thatcher's government, ended Argentina's military junta, and restored British self-image after a decade of imperial retreat. Operationally it was the first sustained test of post-Vietnam Western military technology against a competent regional power and became the canonical case study for naval task-force operations beyond the range of land-based fighter cover.
